title: PM Balen Shah appeals for unity after monster floods batter Nepal; Bihar, UP on high alert
content: A massive flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa district has caused widespread damage and claimed seventeen lives. Over one hundred Indian nationals are reported missing after the sudden surge in the Bhote Koshi River. Many missing individuals are believed to be pilgrims traveling to Tibet for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra. Rescue operations are underway with helicopters and drones searching for the missing people.

title: Gold may hit Rs 15 lakh? Billionaire investor sees 10-fold rise as ‘inevitable’
content: Gold prices have corrected in the last few months from their historic highs after rising meteorically the whole of 2025. This led many to question whether the bull run in the precious metal is over.

title: 'Give supporters reasons to stay': Ramiz Raja warns Pakistan
content: Despite their historical prowess, Pakistan's cricket team is under fire from fans after a disheartening loss to England. Former captain Ramiz Raja noted an alarming rift between the players and supporters. With captain Babar Azam possibly returning, the team hopes to revitalize their batting order. England, fresh off their success, aims to assert dominance in the forthcoming Test at Lord's, while Pakistan desperately seeks a win to equalize the series.

title: Nepal floods: Terrifying videos show homes, buildings and bridges swallowed by raging waters
content: A catastrophic flood from Nepal's Bhotekoshi River has led to severe devastation in Rasuwa district, where mud-laden waters have ravaged homes and bridges. With river currents surging unexpectedly, the fate of many remains uncertain, as reports indicate that over a hundred Indians and thirty-seven NRIs are unaccounted for. Local authorities have declared high alerts, strongly encouraging residents to seek refuge in safer areas.

title: In 1984, NASA sent 3,301 bees to space to see how they built honeycomb
content: In 1984, NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery took thousands of honeybees into space, marking a unique experiment in microgravity. These resilient insects adapted quickly to their extraterrestrial surroundings, building about 200 centimeters of honeycomb in just seven days. Researchers studied the differences in the bees' construction, noting significant variations in cell size and wall thickness between their cosmic creations and those made on Earth.

title: GPS can't work everywhere, so scientists test navigation using cosmic rays
content: Japanese scientists are testing a new navigation system using cosmic ray muons. This system can work in places where GPS signals are unavailable, like underground. Muons can penetrate dense materials, which GPS signals cannot do effectively. Researchers have demonstrated this technology's potential for guiding robots and vehicles. The technology is still under development and requires further refinement for widespread use.

title: Holly Madison refuses to sell 'haunted' LA home, rents it for $9,500 a month
content: Holly Madison has listed her historic Tudor-style Los Angeles home for $9,500 a month after deciding not to sell it. She bought the property for just under $1.5 million in 2012 and has described it as a fairytale-like home. The house was also investigated for paranormal activity in 2021. Madison says she may eventually keep the property for retirement and pass it on to her children.

title: US colleges roll out 3-year bachelor's degrees, could save students $20,000
content: US colleges are increasingly offering three-year bachelor's degree programmes that require 90 credits instead of the traditional 120. The programmes are now available or announced in 26 states, with 119 reduced-credit programmes identified by RAND. Supporters say they can save students time and money, while critics question their impact on learning, professional licensing, graduate admissions and employer acceptance.

title: Anthropic tells SF staff to WFH over security guard strike threat that union denies
content: Anthropic asked employees at its San Francisco offices to work from home on Monday and Tuesday after security contractor Allied Universal warned of a possible strike by its guards. The SEIU, which represents those workers, says it has called no strike authorisation vote and issued no strike threat this week. The union has been negotiating with California security firms over wages and healthcare since April.

title: Delhi reports 138 fresh H1N1 cases in 24 hours; tally crosses 2,400
content: Delhi recorded 138 new H1N1 cases in twenty-four hours, bringing the total to 2,446.  Health officials reviewed hospital preparedness for influenza and other respiratory illnesses.  Hospitals were directed to strengthen emergency services and ensure adequate isolation beds.  The Delhi Medical Association advised mask-wearing and avoiding self-medication for flu symptoms.  Authorities are monitoring trends and hospital readiness to manage patient care effectively.

title: India vs Sri Lanka: A hold, the choke and then the frustrating close
content: India endured a frustrating day in Colombo, allowing Sri Lanka's Pasindu Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis to dictate terms before three late wickets gave the visitors a foothold. With rain cutting the day short, Sonal Dinusha remains the last major hurdle between India and a series clean sweep.

title: Beyond fish in Ayodhya row: Why Nishad vote matters in UP 2027 battle
content: A fish controversy in Uttar Pradesh has highlighted the Nishad community's political significance.  This community's vote has shifted loyalties and remains a key factor for parties.  The BJP seeks to retain its OBC coalition while opposition parties try to gain support.  Nishad leaders have historical ties to epic narratives and social justice movements.  The 2027 elections will test alliances and demands for representation and livelihoods.

title: Patrick Mahomes opens up on knee recovery ahead of Chiefs season opener
content: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, has weighed in on his injury and how he feeld, just days before the regular season begins.

title: Merab Dvalishvili responds to Makhachev’s 'stay quiet' comment after UFC 330 win
content: Merab Dvalishvili clarified his reaction to Islam Makhachev's Russian flag display. He respects Makhachev but cited personal history and Georgian political grievances. Dvalishvili emphasized his opposition to Russian government policies, not its people. Makhachev had previously suggested Petr Yan could silence Dvalishvili. This ongoing discussion highlights the intersection of sports and politics.

title: Max Verstappen’s Max vs 100: Date, venue and how to watch the F1 star’s race
content: Max Verstappen faces a unique go-karting challenge at Silverstone on September 16. He will start last in a field of 100 diverse competitors. The event, Max vs 100, will be broadcast live on Disney+ and ESPN. This race marks a return to Verstappen's early racing roots. Athletes, streamers, and fans will participate in the special event.

title: Raids & kidnapping drills: How Chinese students are prepping for Trump's US
content: Chinese students now receive survival training before attending American universities.  This preparation addresses perceived immigration system unpredictability and potential hostility.  New immigration rules and heightened scrutiny create significant anxiety for families.  Students must now navigate admission, visa, and legal status concerns.  This reflects a shift from academic focus to survival preparation for studying abroad.

title: Sumit’s Comeback: Boxer quits to support family; battles injury to reach Asian Games
content: Haryana boxer Sumit Kundu overcame his father’s death, financial hardship and a career-threatening knee injury to rebuild his career. He quit boxing as a teenager to work as a security guard, but his village helped him return. After winning national and international medals, Kundu missed the Paris Olympics due to injury but made a remarkable comeback, securing his place for the Commonwealth and Asian Games.

title: 'Having suicidal thoughts': Kin recall IIT-D student’s disturbing final week
content: The relatives of Rishikesh Kumar are gravely troubled by his worsening mental health leading up to his tragic death. Reports suggest he felt like a failure and harbored suicidal thoughts. His family believes that administrative interactions caused him significant distress and shame. They were on the verge of pursuing mental health support for him. An external investigation committee is now tasked with reviewing the events that transpired.

title: 'Very rarely do I get chance to play red-ball cricket': Arshdeep
content: India pacer Arshdeep Singh used the Duleep Trophy to prove his readiness for Test cricket after a long gap from red-ball cricket. He took four wickets in North Zone’s 52-run win over West Zone and said he had specifically trained with the red ball. Arshdeep also stressed the value of patience, tactical bowling and domestic cricket in preparing for Tests.

title: Quote of the day by Dolly Parton
content: Dolly Parton, in her inspiring commencement address in 2009, delineated the vital distinction between dreams and mere wishes. She emphasized that dreams are driven by focused efforts and a clear vision for the future, unlike wishes, which tend to lack the necessary determination for realization. Parton urged graduates to embrace personal accountability for their life choices and achievements, rather than shifting responsibility to others.

title: 2nd Test: Rain delays India’s impending series victory over Sri Lanka
content: Sri Lanka ended day four of the second Test at 229 for six after India’s bowlers struck late. Pasindu Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis led the fightback with a 115-run stand, while Sonal Dinusha scored 103 earlier. India’s late wickets put them in control, but rain and bad light halted play, leaving Sri Lanka fighting to avoid defeat on day five.

title: How Hegseth's 'purge' triggered a US Army leadership crisis as Iran war nears six months
content: The US Army faces a leadership void with no permanent chief of staff.  Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has removed several senior officers, impacting leadership continuity.  This occurs while American bases in West Asia endure drone and missile attacks.  The Army's senior civilian official is also expected to depart soon.  This significant personnel churn raises concerns about institutional expertise and decision-making.

title: Starc dethrones Bumrah, becomes No. 1 Test bowler for first time in his career
content: The Australia fast bowler took 10 wickets in the match, including 6/12 in the first innings and 4/39 in the second, helping Australia register an innings and 51-run win and level the World Test Championship series.

title: No ITR filed, then tax notice led to Rs 5.31L refund battle which taxpayer won
content: While completing the assessment, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) rejected the refund claim on the sole ground that a refund could not be claimed through an ITR filed under Section 148 when no original ITR had been filed under Section 139.

title: Karishma Tanna shares postpartum routine; reveals what she eats and drinks
content: In an inspiring revelation, actress Karishma Tanna opened up about her postpartum care routine following the birth of her son on July 29, 2026. She emphasized the importance of nourishing foods and drinks to enhance milk production, while also sharing effective remedies for common postpartum issues like back pain and nipple soreness. Staying well-hydrated and regularly using a belly support belt were key components of her recovery.

title: Cash buyers dominated the US housing boom. Now financed buyers are fighting back
content: Cash purchases in the US housing market are decreasing significantly.  This trend emerges as home sales slow and inventory levels rise.  Price growth has also moderated considerably, benefiting financed buyers.  Financed buyers are now winning competitive bidding situations more frequently.  Cash buyers are becoming less dominant as the market stabilizes.

title: Villages washed away as massive flash floods tear through Nepal - watch
content: A sudden cloudburst triggered severe flooding in the Bhotekoshi River, devastating Nepal's Rasuwa district. Tragically, at least eight people have lost their lives, and several others remain unaccounted for. The disaster has wreaked havoc on local markets, roads, and bridges. Rescue teams are in full swing, employing helicopters from the Nepal army. Authorities are urging residents living near riverbanks in multiple districts to remain vigilant and prepared.

title: Builder told to pay Rs 6 cr to housing society over delay in occupation certificate
content: A Mumbai builder must pay Rs 6 crore to a housing society. This payment is for failing to secure an occupation certificate for over twenty years. Members faced demolition risk and lived without essential services. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered the builder to rectify this. The builder must also obtain the occupation certificate within twelve months.

title: Former Premier League star Akos Buzsaky missing, Hungarian police search
content: Former Premier League footballer Akos Buzsaky is reportedly missing in Hungary. Police have been searching for the ex-Queens Park Rangers midfielder since August 18. His family is also actively trying to locate the 44-year-old former player. Buzsaky has spent considerable time working as a construction contractor in Greece. Hungarian authorities have not released further details regarding his disappearance.

title: 'Played competitive matches against boys': Pak skipper reveals Asia Cup prep
content: Pakistan’s women’s cricket team played full T20 matches against a men’s side during their pre-Asia Cup camp in Lahore to prepare for pressure situations. Captain Fatima Sana believes the unusual training will improve decision-making and composure. Pakistan, who have never won the Women’s Asia Cup, begin their campaign against Thailand on September 1 and face India on September 5.

title: 'ICC letting them get away': Manjrekar wants strict action against Sooryavanshi, Jaiswal
content: The incident happened on the first day after Fernando dismissed Jaiswal. The India opener had hit three boundaries in the over before Fernando bowled him with a delivery that beat his defence.

title: Explained: When it makes sense to take a joint home loan and when it doesn’t
content: When two earning members of a household apply together for a loan, their combined income can potentially improve loan eligibility and help manage repayment burden more efficiently. Most banks and HFCs reiterate that adding an earning family member as a co-applicant can improve their borrowing eligibility.

title: A fatal pact, death note and poison: How a rifle coach came to haunt Andhra family
content: A woman and her parents died after jumping into a river with her son. The woman accused a rifle shooting coach of harassing her and killing her husband. Her son survived the incident after being rescued from the river. The coach was arrested in Meerut after a special investigation team was formed. Police are investigating allegations of murder, threats, and financial control.

title: Rs 30 lakh a month for an intern? India’s trading firms are in a fierce talent war
content: In a bid to attract the brightest minds, high-frequency trading firms in India are ramping up intern compensation to unprecedented levels. This surge in hiring is influenced by stricter regulations on derivatives and a lull in equity market movements. Companies such as Quadeye and Graviton Research Capital are notably enhancing their internship packages, with global firms following suit to secure top quantitative talent from leading institutions.

title: ‘Toxic’ BO day 1 : Yash, Nayanthara, and Kiara Advani starrer gets strong start
content: Yash's new film 'Toxic' has achieved a significant opening day collection across India.  The action drama directed by Geetu Mohandas earned over forty-one crore rupees net.  Audience reactions are divided, praising visuals and Yash's presence but questioning the screenplay.  The Hindi version contributed the most to the film's opening day earnings.  'Toxic' now faces the weekend to sustain its box-office momentum.

title: How do navies hunt submarines? NATO's deadly game of detection beneath the waves
content: NATO navies are focusing on submarine detection and neutralization challenges.  Exercises like Northern Viking 26 highlight coordinated anti-submarine warfare efforts.  Modern warfare relies on advanced acoustic technology and persistent coordination between assets.  India is the only nation to sink a submerged submarine since World War Two.  Submarine and anti-submarine systems continue to advance, making submarine kills more difficult.
